findings.dict_union: Dynamic Any dictionaries now implement | and |= with CPython-like new-dict versus in-place alias behavior, reflected dispatch order and source-size mutation detection.
findings.keyword_calls: Dynamic Any functions, closures, bound methods, callable objects and supported builtins accept keyword arguments with CPython-compatible binding/evaluation order across the measured cases.
findings.keyword_limits: Issue #774 remains open because this is partial: runtime-sized Any unpacking, boxed builtin functions, properties/static/class methods as values and some callable signatures remain outside the supported surface.
findings.typed_sort_limit: dynany_key_none_objects remains a documented deviation: sorting typed object items with a dynamic key that can return None raises TypeError instead of reproducing CPython's ordering behavior.
findings.json_callback_limit: Without sort_keys, a default() callback that clears and repopulates its dictionary observes queued-key traversal rather than CPython's live table cursor. The one-replacement case emits {"a": 1, "z": 9} instead of {"a": 1}; the two-replacement case additionally retains z. PR #839 documents this existing deviation.
findings.imports: No isolated stdlib import gain or regression: 148/460 remains unchanged.
